title: A Wearable Continuous Immune Monitor: Shana Kelley on The Long Run - TimmermanReport.com
author: @ldtimmerman
text:
16Nov2026

Shana Kelley is today’s guest on The Long Run.
Shana is a professor of chemistry at Northwestern University and the president of the Chan Zuckerberg Biohub in Chicago.
Shana Kelley, professor of chemistry, Northwestern University; president, Chan Zuckerberg Biohub Chicago
One of the cool projects she oversees is for a continuous wearable immune monitor. It’s inspired by continuous glucose monitors that have changed the way diabetes is treated and managed. No such device exists today for continuous tracking of inflammation. If her team of chemists, biologists and engineers can pull this off, it would have big implications for research and treatment of immune disorders that affect millions of people. 
The detection of inflammatory proteins was demonstrated in mice and published in Science in December 2024. The next steps to build something suitable for the marketplace will require some kind of industry partnership.
Shana, like a lot of scientists, has taken a circuitous path. I enjoyed hearing her story of how she got to this moment of possibility to seize on new technology tools, and growing knowledge of biology, to spearhead a project with such potential for human health.
